values.TIP: Cylinder head bolt procedure: Tighten all the cylinder head bolts evenly in the tightening order to 30 N·m (3.0 kgf·m, 22 lb·ft). Remove the one bolt according to the tightening order. values.gearing guidance: Secondary reduction ratio = rear sprocket teeth / drive sprocket teeth. Retighten the bolt to 15 N·m (1.5 kgf·m, 11 lb·ft), and then tighten it further to reach the specified angle (60°). Remove the remaining bolts one by one in the same manner and retighten them. Finally, tighten all the bolts to reach the specified angle (60°). Total tightening angle: 60° + 60° = 120° (The first and second time, be sure to apply molybdenum disulfide oil to the bolt threads and seats as well as to both sides of the lock washers.)

values.gearing guidance: Secondary reduction ratio = rear sprocket teeth / drive sprocket teeth. Manual guidance: generally reduce the secondary ratio for a course with a longer straight and increase it for a course with many corners; match the setting to the part of the course that most affects the result, using lap times; on a long straight, set so the engine reaches maximum revolutions toward the end of the straight without over-revving.

values.TIP: Cylinder head bolt procedure: Tighten all the cylinder head tightening bolts evenly in the tightening order to 30 N·m (3.0 kgf·m, 22 lb·ft). Remove the one bolt according to the tightening order. When doing so, do not remove the other bolts. Retighten the bolt to 15 N·m (1.5 kgf·m, 11 lb·ft), and then tighten it further to reach the specified angle (60°). Remove the remaining bolts one by one in the same manner and retighten them. Finally, tighten all the bolts to reach the specified angle (60°). records.statement: Yamaha's 2020 YZ250F owner's service manual lists a periodic maintenance chart in race/hour intervals (after break-in, every race about 2.5 h, every third race about 7.5 h, every fifth race about 12.5 h) with 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 API service SG type or higher, JASO standard MA engine oil (0.73 L (0.77 US qt, 0.64 Imp.qt) at an oil change, 0.75 L (0.79 US qt, 0.66 Imp.qt) with filter), NGK/LMAR9E-J plug gapped 0.6–0.7 mm (0.024–0.028 in), and Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 in the fork.

records.statement: Yamaha's 2020 YZ250F owner's service manual lists optional fork springs from 4.5 to 5.1 N/mm (standard 4.7 N/mm) and shock springs from 52 to 60 N/mm (standard 56 N/mm), with 90–100 mm rear sag, 290 cm³ (9.80 US oz, 10.23 Imp.oz) standard fork oil amount and 50/13 standard gearing (rear sprockets 47T-52T).

values.gearing guidance: Secondary reduction ratio = rear sprocket teeth / drive sprocket teeth. Manual guidance: generally reduce the secondary ratio for a course with a longer straight and increase it for a course with many corners; match the setting to the part of the course that most affects the result, using lap times; on a long straight, set so the engine reaches maximum revolutions toward the end of the straight without over-revving.
values.rear spring preload standard: spring turned in 4.0 mm (0.16 in) from its free length
values.sag measurement reference: rear wheel axle center to rear fender holding bolt
values.rear spring preload minimum: spring turned in 1.5 mm (0.06 in) from its free length
values.rear spring preload maximum: spring turned in 18.0 mm (0.71 in) from its free length
values.fork oil amount change step: 5 cm³ (0.2 US oz, 0.2 Imp.oz) increments or decrements; too little oil -> noise at full rebound / pressure felt by rider; too much -> air spring too stiff
values.fork: after fitting a softer spring: rebound damping out (softer) 1-2 clicks; compression damping in (harder) 1-2 clicks
values.fork: after fitting a stiffer spring: rebound damping in 1-2 clicks; compression damping out 1-2 clicks
values.shock: after fitting a softer spring: set sag to 90–100 mm, run with rebound adjuster 1-2 clicks out, then readjust
values.shock: after fitting a stiffer spring: set sag to 90–100 mm, run with rebound adjuster 1-2 clicks in, then readjust; if rebound changes compression, correct by decreasing compression damping
values.shock length warning: never use a replacement rear shock whose overall length "a" exceeds the standard

values.fork chart: unsmooth movement over entir: check outer/inner tube for bends, dents or scars; replace slide metal / piston metal for extended use; retighten lower bracket to specified torque
values.fork chart: poor initial movement: rebound CCW about 2 clicks; apply grease to oil seal wall

values.fork chart: obtrusive front, tending to: compression CCW about 2 clicks; set rear sag 90–95 mm (3.5–3.7 in) (upper rear posture); softer spring; decrease oil about 5-10 cm³

values.shock chart: stiff, tending to sink: rebound CCW about 2 clicks; set sag 90–100 mm
values.shock chart: spongy and unstable: rebound CW about 2 clicks; low compression CW about 1 click; stiffer spring
values.shock chart: heavy and dragging: rebound CCW about 2 clicks; softer spring

records.notes: The manual gives spring options by rate (SOFT to STIFF) with part numbers and I.D. marks but no rider-weight table; choose springs so the 90–100 mm sag can be reached.
